fixes.explanation: Glad is the word, friend. Isaiah says "The wilderness and the dry land will be glad…" (Isaiah 35:1). I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and glad was not the word I'd have picked.

Ashamed is a swing and a miss, but I see why dry land might make you think of something sad. The verse goes the other direction. The wilderness and the dry land will be glad, and the desert will rejoice (Isaiah 35:1).
Afraid sounds reasonable for a dry, empty place. Isaiah doesn't say that, though. He says the wilderness and the dry land will be glad (Isaiah 35:1).
The LORD's glory, yes. Isaiah says, "They will see the glory of the LORD, the splendor of our God." (Isaiah 35:2). The blooming is wonderful, and you've got the right eyes on the right thing.
That's the message. Isaiah says to tell those with anxious hearts, "Be strong, do not fear!" (Isaiah 35:4). Five words and a whole lot of comfort. Those are the words for anxious hearts.

True, and it's right there in the verse. Isaiah says, "Then the eyes of the blind will be opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped." (Isaiah 35:5). Blind eyes and deaf ears sit side by side. Eyes and ears, both covered.
Leap like a deer, that's it. Isaiah says, "Then the lame will leap like a deer…" (Isaiah 35:6). I'd love to see that, though I'd need to get my base out of the way.
Resting is a sensible guess, and rest has its place. But Isaiah paints a much bigger picture. He says, "Then the lame will leap like a deer…" (Isaiah 35:6).
Being carried home is kind-hearted, and I see where it came from. The verse has something livelier in mind, though. Isaiah says, "Then the lame will leap like a deer…" (Isaiah 35:6).

Cedars, cypresses and pines do show up in Isaiah (Isaiah 41:19), so I see why you'd reach for them. Not in this verse, though. Isaiah says, "In the haunt where jackals once lay, there will be grass and reeds and papyrus." (Isaiah 35:7). It's a watery list, not a forest.
I get why it seems like fools would wander onto any road. I've wandered into plenty of wrong rooms myself. But Isaiah says the opposite: "…fools will not stray onto it." (Isaiah 35:8).

False, and well spotted. Isaiah says, "And there will be a highway called the Way of Holiness. The unclean will not travel it—only those who walk in the Way—and fools will not stray onto it." (Isaiah 35:8). The fools part is right there at the end of the verse.

With singing, yes. Isaiah says, "So the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing, crowned with everlasting joy." (Isaiah 35:10). Crowned with everlasting joy is how the verse describes them as they come in.
Weeping is an understandable guess for a homecoming. But Isaiah says the redeemed "…will return and enter Zion with singing…" (Isaiah 35:10). The same verse says sorrow and sighing will flee.
Silence is a fair guess for a solemn moment. Isaiah paints something louder, though. The redeemed "…will return and enter Zion with singing…" (Isaiah 35:10). In that verse, they come in singing.
